subject: Re: AcmeCorp security discovery / subprocessor list & SOC 2 status
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com>, Bob Taylor <bob.taylor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: AcmeCorp discovery 	6 security/compliance follow-up

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for the call this morning 	6 good to learn more about AcmeCorp's embedding pipeline and the latency targets you mentioned. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on security/compliance items we discussed: 

- SOC 2: You asked about our current SOC 2 posture. We have a SOC 2 Type II audit in progress (controls period completed for 2025); our auditor work is scheduled for Q4 2026 and we expect a final Type II report by end of Q4. I can share the last Type I summary and a controls summary now.
- Subprocessors: You asked for our subprocessor list and a short explanation of data boundaries. I can provide a CSV listing our current subprocessors and their roles (cloud infra, telemetry, SSO, monitoring, managed DB).
- Vendor security questionnaire: happy to complete AcmeCorp's security questionnaire. If you can share the questionnaire link or attach the doc, we'll fill and return within 3 business days.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will send the subprocessor CSV + a short SOC 2 status note by EOD tomorrow.
2) Please loop in Legal (cc'd Bob) with the DPA and any specific clauses you need to confirm (data residency, access controls, retention).
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 45-min technical security deep dive next week with Rishi (security engineer) and Dev (infrastructure) to walk architecture and boundary controls.

Thanks 	6 I'll follow up with the attachments.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick notes from our side:

- SOC 2: Good to know the timeline 	6 we need Type II or an auditor attestation before procurement can finish. Is there a controls/coverage matrix you can share in the meantime?
- Subprocessors: please include cloud provider regions (us-west-2, us-east-1) and whether any subprocessors process PII or customer data in plaintext. Also call out any subprocessors with cross-border transfers.
- Questionnaire: I'll attach the security questionnaire (PDF) to this thread and have Legal track the DPA.

We'll plan on the 45-min deep dive; can you do Tue 8/18 or Wed 8/19 PST? Please confirm attendees and we will send a calendar invite.

alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com>, Bob Taylor <bob.taylor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-13T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeCorp discovery 	6 subprocessor list and SOC2 details (attachments)

Hi Alice / team,

Attached is the subprocessor CSV and a short SOC 2 status note. High-level notes included in the CSV:
- Cloud infra: Google Cloud (primary compute, us-west-2, us-east-1) and AWS (backup, us-east-1) 	6 both under standard customer-managed encryption in transit and at rest.
- Storage/DB: Managed Postgres (Cloud SQL) 	6 logical separation per customer, no cross-customer data mixing.
- Telemetry & monitoring: Datadog (metrics/logs) 	6 we redact request payloads and only ship telemetry metadata; full logs with request content are not sent to Datadog.
- Authentication: Okta for SSO 	6 we do not store passwords; session tokens are short-lived.
- PCI/HIPAA: We are not handling card payments directly. For HIPAA customers we offer Private deployment options and a BAAs discussion; public hosted offering is used by non-PHI customers only.

I've also attached a filled copy of your questionnaire (redwood_vendor_questionnaire_filled.pdf) for the first pass; please review and flag any areas that need expansion.

Attachments (stubs): redwood_subprocessors_2026.csv, SOC2_TypeII_status_note_2026.txt, redwood_vendor_questionnaire_filled.pdf

We can provide a short export mapping fields that are considered PII vs non-PII if that would help your Privacy team.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--
Note: CSV columns include: subprocessor_name, role, data_processed, region, contract_clause_reference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-13T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeCorp discovery 	6 architecture/telemetry question

Hi Alice 	6 looping in Rishi (security) and myself to handle any infra-level questions during the deep dive. Quick technical points up front:

- KV cache and inference payloads: we persist KV cache on encrypted block storage per instance and do not share KV caches across customers.
- Prefix caching: only model tokens used for prompt prefixing are cached; we do not store customer prompts in long-term analytics without explicit opt-in.
- Dataflow to telemetry: request metadata and anonymized latency metrics are sent to Datadog. We can provide sanitized examples of logs if needed for your legal/privacy review.

Happy to cover these in more detail on the call.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmecorp.com>

- Can you confirm data retention default policy and options for customer-specific retention settings?

We'll schedule the security deep dive for Tue 2026-08-18 10:00 AM PST; invite will go out from our side. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Alice
